title: Kestrel and the Alibi
premise: August Ravensworth, the reclusive archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, has spent her life cataloguing other people's legacies while avoiding her own. When a stranger is found dead in the locked crypt wearing clothes stolen from August's closet, she becomes both suspect and sleuth, forced to confront the inheritance she fled thirty years ago: her family's fortune, and the night her mother died, when every alibi in the village was quietly rewritten. As August unpicks the forged timelines, she discovers the dead woman was the last person who could have proven August's own innocence, and that her found family at the cathedral includes the killer. In the end, August trades her invisibility for the truth, claiming both the inheritance and the belonging she never believed she deserved.
about_author: Astrid Montrose is the pen name of a former cathedral tour guide who spent a decade listening to tourists ask what was behind locked doors. She writes mysteries about quiet people who notice everything, from a cottage within earshot of church bells.

chapters.title: The Clothes in the Crypt
chapters.summary: August's POV. Opening the crypt for a routine inspection, August finds a dead woman in a locked chamber, dressed in August's own missing cardigan and scarf. Detective Inspector Hale, who remembers her three unofficial 'accident' investigations, treats her as witness, suspect, or asset. The victim carries an old photograph of August's mother. Emotional beat: dread and the collapse of August's careful invisibility.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: August's POV, with flashbacks. August matches the victim, Marlowe Quinn, to a former housemaid at Ravensworth Hall who vanished the week after her mother's death. Digging into parish records and Marlowe's rented room, she finds a diary claiming her mother's 'accident' was murder, and that five villagers coordinated their alibis. One of them now works at the cathedral. Emotional beat: the past pressing in, trust beginning to fracture.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: August's POV. August sets a trap by letting slip that the diary's final page, naming the killer, survives. That night someone breaks into the archive; August catches verger Tom Ellery, her closest friend, holding the diary and the missing clothes. Tom confesses his father was one of the five, that Marlowe came to blackmail him, and that he only meant to frighten her in the crypt. Emotional beat: betrayal, and August's grief at losing her found family.

chapters.title: Kestrel
chapters.summary: August's POV. Tom's story doesn't fully fit: the crypt was locked from outside, and only one person holds both keys, the dean, whose alibi thirty years ago was the original forgery. Confronting him in the crypt, August records his confession as he admits killing her mother and, when Marlowe recognized the truth, killing her too. Hale arrests the dean; Tom's lesser role earns mercy. August accepts her inheritance and stays. Emotional beat: belonging, finally chosen.
